motivation: Pooled pre-loss focal history predicts Thalassia re-recording, whereas the frozen bare-loss subgroup does not. Test whether the local-history effect is stronger when another seagrass remains in the focal-loss year.

primary_population.sequence_rule: same frozen 259 three-year exact-point Thalassia-loss sequences
primary_population.pre_loss_run_length: immediately consecutive consensus years with Thalassia present ending in the source year
primary_population.continuity_state: loss_year_vegetated = 1 if another seagrass remains at t+1, else 0

model.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the same meter mark in the recovery year
model.preprocessing: node-center pre-loss run length, then StandardScaler numeric terms; OneHot node identity

primary_hypothesis.statement: The positive association between pre-loss local Thalassia history and one-year re-recording is stronger when the focal-loss year remains vegetated by another seagrass.
primary_hypothesis.estimator: coefficient of the standardized centered-run-length × loss-year-vegetated interaction
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for the interaction coefficient > 0

secondary_descriptive: fitted centered-run-length coefficient among vegetated sequences only
fitted centered-run-length coefficient among bare sequences only
return fraction by loss-year vegetation state

interpretation.supported: Local persistence history and above-ground community continuity interact positively, consistent with a compound resilience state in which historical local occupancy is expressed most strongly when seagrass habitat continuity is retained.
interpretation.unsupported: The apparent contrast between pooled and bare-subgroup history effects does not yield a robust interaction; the bare null may reflect limited sample size or broader site-state differences.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc interaction test motivated by already-opened pooled and bare-subgroup results.
A positive interaction would not prove facilitation by alternative seagrasses; both continuity and history may index persistent microsite quality.
A positive interaction would not identify clonal/rhizome memory without direct below-ground measurements.
Return is recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not alter the interaction term, history definition, node-centering, controls, model, minima, or support threshold after opening the interaction endpoint.
